{{center block/s}}</noinclude><ref follow="p387_6">[[w:King Tai of Zhou|king Thâi]], who came with him from [[w:Bin (city)|Pin]]. She is here called ''K''âu, as having married the lord of [[w:Predynastic Zhou|''K''âu]].</ref>A wife becoming the House of {{tooltip|''K''âu|Zhōu}}.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
{{tooltip|Thâi Sze|Tài Sì}}<ref>[[w:Tai Si|Thâi Sze]], the wife of [[w:King Wen of Zhou|Wăn]], we are told in [[Sacred Books of the East/Volume 3/The Shih/The Major Odes of the Kingdom/Decade 1/Ode 2|ode 2]], was from the state of [[w:zh:有莘氏|Hsin]]. The surname [[w:Si (surname)|Sze]] shows that its lords must have been descended from the [[w:Yu the Great|Great Yü]].</ref> inherited her excellent fame,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And from her came a hundred sons<ref>We are not to suppose that [[w:Tai Si|Thâi Sze]] had herself a hundred sons. She had ten, and her freedom from jealousy so encouraged the fruitfulness of the harem, that all the sons born in it are ascribed to her.</ref>.

He conformed to the example of his ancestors,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And their spirits had no occasion for complaint.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Their spirits had no occasion for dissatisfaction;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And his example acted on his wife,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Extended to his brethren,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And was felt by all the clans and states.

Full of harmony was he in his palace;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Full of reverence in the ancestral temple.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
{{anchor|unseen}}Unseen (by men), he still felt that he was under inspection<ref>Where there was no human eye to observe him, [[w:King Wen of Zhou|Wăn]] still felt that he was open to the observation of spiritual beings.</ref>:{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Unweariedly he maintained his virtue.

Though he could not prevent (some) great calamities,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
His brightness and magnanimity were without stain.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Without previous instruction he did what was right;{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
Without admonition he went on (in the path of goodness).

So, grown up men became virtuous (through him),{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And young men made (constant) attainments.{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
(Our) ancient prince never felt weariness,{{page other|{{wsp|0.5em}}|{{br}}}}
And from him were the fame and eminence of his officers.
